name: Tierce Bells
description: Cast bells whose third is a control: set it anywhere from narrow minor to a fourth, let it follow the key of the music, or let it glide from one third to another inside a single strike.

params.name: Bell
params.description: Which kind of bell is rung. Each has its own partials, striker and way of dying; a rubbed bell swells while its key is held. Heard from the next bell.

params.name: Tierce
params.description: How far the bell's third lies above its note. Low is a narrow minor third, the middle sits between minor and major, and the top is a fourth.

params.name: Follow
params.description: With Key each bell takes the third that Root and Scale give its note, major or minor. A note outside the scale takes the Tierce knob, as every bell does when off.

params.name: Root
params.description: The note the scale starts on when Follow is on. Bells that are ringing glide to their new thirds.

params.name: Scale
params.description: The scale that decides which bells ring major and which minor when Follow is on. Bells that are ringing glide to their new thirds.

params.name: Lean
params.description: Starts each strike's third above or below its place and lets it glide there, like a suspension that resolves inside one bell. Glide sets how long it takes.

params.name: Glide
params.description: How long a third takes to reach its place, after a strike that leans and after Tierce, Root or Scale moves under bells that are ringing.

params.name: Hum pitch
params.description: Pitch of the low hum tone against the note. The centre is an octave below; higher nears a minor seventh below, as in older bells, and lower passes a ninth.

params.name: Hum level
params.description: How loud the low hum tone under the note is. At zero the bell has no hum.

params.name: Quint
params.description: How loud the fifth inside the bell is. At zero the fifth is gone, which leaves the third by itself.

params.name: Upper
params.description: How loud the partials from the octave up are. Low leaves hum, note and third; high rings bright, with the third heard again an octave higher.

params.name: Decay
params.description: How long the hum of a bell rings. The partials above it die sooner, by an amount the kind of bell and Damping set.

params.name: Damping
params.description: How much sooner the upper partials die than the hum. Low keeps the whole bell ringing; high goes dull quickly, like a heavy or a cracked bell.

params.name: Hardness
params.description: How hard the clapper is. Soft wakes the low partials gently; hard brings a quick, bright strike. On a rubbed bell it brings up the upper partials.

params.name: Doublet
params.description: Splits the main partials into pairs a little apart, so they beat at this rate. A true round bell is still; a worn one warbles.

params.name: Release
params.description: How quickly a bell is choked when its key is let go. At zero it rings on untouched; at the top a hand stops it.

params.name: Spread
params.description: Places the partials across the stereo field. With more of it the beating pairs turn from side to side between the speakers.

params.name: Volume
params.description: Overall output level of the instrument.

origin.note: Written for live-mix on cpp/kit. Each partial is a rotating complex one-pole, the form modal-bells uses; partial names and places are the textbook ones of a tuned bell (hum, prime, tierce, quint, nominal, deciem), and the third is a parameter. Levels and ring times are voiced by measurement, not taken from a particular bell.
